rationale: The assistant went straight to the right area with a proportionate, answerable check ('can you see two springs... taut or slack?') and, once the customer reported a loose right-hand spring, a twang and tension remaining on the left, correctly concluded 'the right-hand spring has snapped' and recommended replacement with an engineer, matching the hidden truth. It stayed faithful to the evidence, hedged appropriately ('probably', 'suggests'), and made no compatibility claims. Weaknesses: it never asked for the full model number, did not mention replacing springs in pairs or isolating power/water before the unit is pulled out, and did not establish whether the customer could pull the machine out before defaulting to an engineer; the claim that fitting a spring requires 'removing the door assembly' is also slightly loose.
